item.title: Understanding the 12 Days of Christmas in Orthodoxy
item.description: In the Orthodox Church, the Twelve Days of Christmas form a sacred bridge between the Nativity of Christ on December 25 and His Baptism (Theophany) on January 6—a time of great joy honoring the Incarnation, early martyrs, apostles, and saints. item.title: Festive Visit: Cretan Traditions Bring Christmas Joy to Greece's Ministry of Tourism
item.description: The historic Club of Vraka-Wearers of Crete brought festive joy to Greece's Ministry of Tourism on Christmas Eve, singing traditional Cretan Christmas carols and dancing with Minister Olga Kefalogianni, who proudly joined in celebrating the island's rich heritage. item.title: Tragedy in Turkey: Greek Flight Attendant Maria Pappa Among Victims of Fatal Plane Crash
item.description: Maria Pappa, a 42-year-old Greek flight attendant with nearly 20 years of experience, tragically died in the December 23, 2025, crash of a Falcon 50 private jet near Ankara, Turkey. The aircraft, operated by Harmony Jets, was carrying Libya's Chief of General Staff Mohammed Ali Ahmed al-Haddad and senior officials when it reported an electrical failure and crashed, killing all eight on board. item.title: Netanyahu's Christmas Eve Message: Israel the Only Middle East Country Where Christians Thrive
item.description: In his Christmas Eve 2025 message from Jerusalem, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu declared Israel the only Middle East country where Christians thrive, contrasting it with persecution elsewhere, including a recent arson attack on a Christmas tree in Jenin and the decline of Bethlehem's Christian population under PA control. item.description: Stefanos Tsitsipas and Maria Sakkari, both former world No. 3s, return for their fourth consecutive United Cup, leading Greece in Group E in Perth against Great Britain and Japan, fueled by strong fan support and their proven on-court chemistry. item.title: Controversial Giant Christmas Tree Illuminated Near Crete's Samaria Gorge
item.description: A 45-meter metal Christmas tree, lit up near the entrance to Crete's Samaria Gorge on December 21, 2025, attracted thousands but sparked outrage for its placement in a protected area, leading authorities to declare it unauthorized.
